Application.Evaluate("WSD(...)") returns the literal string Fetching... and never resolves: first call 1513ms (the Wind request), subsequent calls 3-19ms cache reads of the same placeholder across 40 polls over 122s

Single-cell FormulaArray is NOT honoured as a CSE array formula under PowerShell 5.1 COM binding: IsInArray stays False and CurrentArray is always 1x1, so multi-cell spill is invisible to automation. The two-step helper-grid workaround also fails to copy the spill.

The only path the WDF add-in honours under COM automation is Range.Formula + Application.Calculate() + polling: the Fetching... placeholder is replaced within ~5-6s. This is the path the authorised run used.

The add-in accepts WSD formulas but never delivers data: the full payload formula returns 无法读取数据！(cannot read data) on every attempt for every instrument. Parameter-form enumeration confirms the field argument is not honoured: WSD("CU.SHF","CLOSE",...) and WSD("CU.SHF","Close",...) both return the bare date 2025-01-02, while WSD("CU.SHF",1,...) and WSD("CU.SHF","CLOSE;OPEN",...) return a single bare value 73280 with no spill. WS() returns #NAME? and WSS() returns #VALUE!, so this add-in exposes only WSD and it does not honour the requested field list.

Wind terminal API bridge layer is not activated, so the Excel-WDF chain cannot serve data. wmain.exe (824) and initwapi.exe (14188) are running, the WDF.Addin is loaded and connected in the background Excel, and WSD responds - but no data grid is returned.
